new.n: Summerwind ruins (Lamont's "Lilac Hills"), West Bay Lake: LOOK ONLY (spot approximate)
new.pl: Wisconsin shore of West Bay Lake (Cisco Chain), near the sec. 18/19 line, T43N R9E, Town of Land O' Lakes
new.v: Look only: private, fenced and posted
new.st: Robert Patterson Lamont of Chicago bought a small lakeside lodge-and-cabins retreat here in 1916. He was an American Steel Foundries executive and later Hoover's Secretary of Commerce. He rebuilt it as a 20-room, two-storey summer house with big stone fireplaces and called it Lilac Hills; Hoover and Harding are said to have visited. Lamont died in 1948, after the family had given up the house. The Keefer family owned it next, and the Hinshaws lived there about six months around 1970. It stood empty from the early 1970s, and Raymond Bober's 1979 book The Carver Effect and a 1980 Life magazine piece made "Summerwind" famous. In 1985 the town tried to burn it, and the owner boarded it up instead. In fall 1986 new owners bought it from the Lillian Keefer estate for a B&B and fenced and posted it. Lightning set it on fire on 19 June 1988, and the servants' quarters and laundry burned with it: "Everything is gone except two chimneys and the cement and stone patio." Treasure angle: Bober claimed a 1700s "Carver deed" was hidden in the foundation, and seekers tore at the stone basement walls; the deed story is folklore and nothing was ever found. The intruder-shooting and madness stories are legend. SPOT APPROXIMATE: the pin is on the only high-ground building group on the Wisconsin shore of the 1981 topo, which fits the 1988 paper's "on a high hill"; it is good to about 150 m. The Wikipedia coordinate is only the lake's GNIS centre, on the Michigan side.
new.t: LOOK ONLY. Private, fenced and posted: look from the lake or the road unless you have the owner's written permission. Get the current owner from the Vilas County land records before you ask.
